query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The formation of a fine dispersion of Cu‐rich nanoprecipitates in a FeNiCrCoCu high‐entropy alloy coating is the primary factor governing its wear resistance and microscopic deformation during high‐temperature sliding: these precipitates strengthen the matrix, impede dislocation motion, and stabilize a protective tribolayer, thereby reducing wear volume and subsurface plastic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu HEA coating in the as‐deposited (single‐phase solid solution) condition on a steel substrate
generation.intervention: Post‐deposition annealing at 600 °C for 2 hours in vacuum to induce Cu‐rich nanoprecipitation
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests at 600 °C, 5 N normal load, 5 mm/s sliding speed, 1000 cycles
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale Cu‐rich precipitate dispersion within the HEA matrix
generation.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening increases hardness and impedes dislocation motion under sliding, while enhanced oxygen scavenging by Cu‐rich regions stabilizes a low‐shear tribolayer
generation.predicted_outcome: Annealed coating will exhibit higher hardness, lower wear volume, and a shallower subsurface plastic deformation zone relative to the as‐deposited baseline
generation.baseline: As‐deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating without detectable nanoprecipitates
generation.boundary: Predictions apply for annealing treatments of 1–4 h at 500–700 °C and sliding loads up to 10 N in air
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitude of wear reduction and deformation‐zone depth reduction is uncertain due to lack of direct prior measurements

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeNiCrCoCu coatings on steel: one as‐deposited, one annealed at 600 °C for 2 h. Perform sliding wear tests at 600 °C, 5 N, 5 mm/s, 1000 cycles.
measurements: Subsurface plastic deformation zone depth (cross‐sectional SEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed coating does not show a statistically significant decrease in wear volume and subsurface deformation‐zone depth compared to the as‐deposited baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
